title: Finite affinoid maps are finite on spectral unit balls over an algebraically closed field
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], complete for a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Let $A,B\ne0$ be commutative unital affinoid $K$-algebras: each is a quotient of a finite-variable Tate algebra of restricted series [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with its affinoid Banach topology. Assume $B$ is reduced. For $H=A,B$ define $\rho_H(h)=\sup_\chi|\chi(h)|$, with $\chi:H\to K$ running over continuous unital $K$-algebra homomorphisms, and put $H_{\le1}=\{h\in H:\rho_H(h)\le1\}$. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a continuous $K$-algebra homomorphism satisfying $\rho_B(\varphi(a))\le\rho_A(a)$ for all $a\in A$. Assume $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module through $\varphi$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $B_{\le1}$ is a finitely generated $A_{\le1}$-module through the restriction of $\varphi$.

source.place: Section 6.4.1, Corollaries 5 and 6, algebraically closed base and reduced target case. Independently checked in Conrad perfectoid seminar, Lecture 12, paragraph following Example 12.2.5, PDF p.2: a finite affinoid map is finite on power-bounded subrings in this case. The spectral unit balls equal the power-bounded subrings for reduced affinoids. Primary seminar PDF read online 2026-10-24; local archival copies of BGR and Lecture 12 WANTED.

proof.text: First identify the character supremum in the statement with the maximal-ideal supremum $\sigma_H$ of [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], for every nonzero affinoid $H$ used below. Each maximal residue field is finite over the algebraically closed $K$, hence is $K$ as a $K$-algebra. Its residue character is continuous: its absolute value is bounded by $\sigma_H$, which in turn is bounded by any Tate quotient Gauss norm. Conversely, a unital $K$-character is onto $K$, so has maximal kernel and is this residue character. Thus $\rho_H=\sigma_H$, even for nonreduced $H$. The cited lemma supplies finiteness, contraction for every affinoid homomorphism, and equality with the Gauss norm on a Tate algebra. Directly from the character formula, $\rho_H(h+h')\le\max(\rho_H(h),\rho_H(h'))$, the unit balls are subrings, $\rho_H(hh')\le\rho_H(h)\rho_H(h')$ and $\rho_H(ah)=|a|\rho_H(h)$ for $a\in K$. In particular the stipulated restriction of $\varphi$ is a ring map.

source.place: Section 6.2.1, supremum seminorm; use of the given spectral balls in Corollary 6.4.1/5. Primary BGR scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a Tate presentation $A=T_r/I$; $I$ is proper since $A\ne0$. By [lem-trf-tate-normalization-lift] choose $T=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle$ and a finite injective map $j:T\to A$. Write $G$ for its Gauss norm. By [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], $\rho_A(j(t))\le G(t)$. The composite $T\to A\to B$ makes $B$ finite over $T$: if $a_l$ generate $A$ over $T$ and $b_k$ generate $B$ over $A$, the products $\varphi(a_l)b_k$ generate, by expanding each coefficient in $b=\sum_k\varphi(a_k')b_k$. For this action $\rho_B(tb)\le G(t)\rho_B(b)$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.4.1/3, reduction of the source to a Tate algebra, printed pp.251–252. Primary BGR scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affinoid-minimal-component-norm] to the reduced, nonzero $B$. Obtain nonzero affinoid domains $C_i=B/\mathfrak p_i$ and an injective map $q:B\to P=\prod_i C_i$ with $\rho_B(b)=\max_i\rho_{C_i}(q_i(b))$, using step 1 to identify the seminorm conventions. Each $C_i$ is finite over $T$, since images of a finite generating family of $B$ still generate its quotient. By [lem-trf-affinoid-spectral-banach-norm], applied to each nonzero reduced $C_i$, these component functions are norms. Give $P$ the maximum norm. Each $T$-action is contractive for $G$, by the character inequalities from step 1, so $q$ is an isometric $T$-linear inclusion.

source.place: Theorem 6.4.1/3, general reduced case and Lemma 6.2.1/3, printed p.252. Primary BGR scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For each $i$, let $J_i=\ker(T\to C_i)$, a proper ideal. Apply [lem-trf-tate-normalization-lift] to $T/J_i$. It supplies an injective map $\alpha_i:S_i=K\langle W_1,\ldots,W_{e_i}\rangle\to T$ for which $S_i\to T/J_i$ is finite and injective. The induced $T/J_i\to C_i$ is injective by the definition of $J_i$ and finite: the $T$-generators of $C_i$ still generate after replacing each coefficient by its class modulo $J_i$. Thus $S_i\to C_i$ is finite and injective, with finiteness given by the double-sum calculation of step 2. The source-to-source maps satisfy $G(\alpha_i(s))\le G_i(s)$ by [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], where $G_i$ is the Gauss norm of $S_i$. By [lem-trf-tate-fraction-orthogonal-spectral-norm], the norm $\rho_{C_i}$ extends to an $F_i=\operatorname{Frac}(S_i)$-vector-space norm $N_i$ on $L_i=\operatorname{Frac}(C_i)$ with a finite orthogonal $F_i$-basis $v_{ik}$. This lemma applies to the domain $C_i$ and the finite injective map just constructed; no separability assumption is used.

source.place: Theorem 6.4.1/3, domain case: normalization of the source modulo its kernel, and the cartesian fraction field, printed pp.251–252. Primary BGR scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

A nonzero Gauss norm of a restricted series is the absolute value of one coefficient: choose a nonzero coefficient $c$ and the threshold $|c|/2>0$; the coefficients exceeding it form a finite nonempty set, so their maximum is attained, bounds all remaining coefficients and is therefore the Gauss norm. Hence $|F_i^	imes|=|K^	imes|$, and as $K$ is algebraically closed every element of $|K^	imes|$ has its $l$th roots in $|K^	imes|$. source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.4.1/3, enclosing the finite domain module in a cartesian Tate lattice, printed p.252; value group of the spectral norm from Corollaries 6.4.1/4-5, p.251. Primary BGR scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-tate-submodule-norm-controlled-generators] with $D=S_i$, $s=n_i$ and the $S_i$-submodule $\Lambda_i'=\beta_i^{-1}(C_i)\subseteq S_i^{n_i}$, whose maximum Gauss norm is the norm $\|\cdot\|$ of that node. It gives $v'_1,\ldots,v'_{h_i}\in\Lambda_i'$ with $\|v'_m\|=1$ such that each $x\in\Lambda'_i$ is $\sum_mf_mv'_m$ with $G_i(f_m)\le\|x\|$. Put $x_{im}=\beta_i(v'_m)\in C_i$. Since $N_i$ restricts to $\rho_{C_i}$ on $C_i$ (step 4, with step 1), step 5 gives $\rho_{C_i}(x_{im})=1$, and $\rho_{C_i}(\beta_i(x))=\|x\|$. For $c\in C_i$ put $x=\beta_i^{-1}(c)$: then $c=\sum_mf_mx_{im}$ with $G_i(f_m)\le\rho_{C_i}(c)$, while the ultrametric inequality and $N_i(fz)=|f|_{F_i}N_i(z)$ give $\rho_{C_i}(c)\le\max_mG_i(f_m)$. Thus $\rho_{C_i}(c)=\max_mG_i(f_m)$ for this representation.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.4.1/3, submodule of the cartesian lattice via Theorem 5.2.7/7 and Corollary 5.2.7/11, printed pp.208-212, 252; the unit-weight case cited here is Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry, Section 1.3, Corollary 10. Primary BGR scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
These families work over the common $T$. The map $S_i\to C_i$ is the composite of $\alpha_i$ with $T\to T/J_i\to C_i$, so step 6 gives $c=\sum_m\alpha_i(f_m)x_{im}$, and the action inequality of step 3 and contraction of $\alpha_i$ from step 4 give
$$\rho_{C_i}(c)\le\max_mG(\alpha_i(f_m))\le\max_mG_i(f_m)=\rho_{C_i}(c).$$
Thus equality holds throughout. Put each $x_{im}$ in the $i$th factor of $P$, with zero in every other factor, and index the concatenated family by the finite set $R$ of pairs $(i,m)$. Let $\pi:T^R\to P$, $(t_{im})\mapsto\sum t_{im}x_{im}$. It is $T$-linear, $\|\pi(t)\|_P\le\max G(t_{im})$ by the ultrametric and action inequalities, and every $p\in P$ is $\pi(t)$ for some $t$ with $\max G(t_{im})=\|p\|_P$: represent each component separately and take the maximum over $R$.

source.place: Theorem 6.4.1/3, transport of pseudo-cartesian generators from the normalizing Tate algebra and finite direct sums; Lemma 5.2.7/4(a), printed pp.209,251–252. Primary BGR scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The isometric image $q(B)\subseteq P$ is a $T$-submodule, so $\Lambda''=\pi^{-1}(q(B))\subseteq T^R$ is a $T$-submodule. Apply [lem-trf-tate-submodule-norm-controlled-generators] with $D=T$ and $s=|R|$. It gives $v''_1,\ldots,v''_g\in\Lambda''$ of maximum Gauss norm $1$ such that each $\tau=(\tau_r)_{r\in R}\in\Lambda''$ is $\sum_hf_hv''_h$ with $G(f_h)\le\max_{r\in R}G(\tau_r)$. Since $q$ is injective, define $y_h\in B$ by $q(y_h)=\pi(v''_h)$; as $q$ is isometric, $\rho_B(y_h)\le1$. For $b\in B$ choose by step 7 a $t\in T^R$ with $\pi(t)=q(b)$ and $\max G(t_{im})=\rho_B(b)$. Then $t\in\Lambda''$, so $t=\sum_hf_hv''_h$ with $G(f_h)\le\rho_B(b)$. Applying the $T$-linear maps $\pi$ and $q^{-1}$ on $q(B)$ gives $b=\sum_hf_hy_h$, where $T$ acts on $B$ through $\varphi\circ j$.

source.place: Theorem 6.4.1/3, reduced case, last sentence: Corollary 5.2.7/11 for the embedded submodule, printed p.252. Primary BGR scan read online 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $b\in B_{\le1}$ take the representation $b=\sum_hf_hy_h$ of step 8. Every $G(f_h)\le\rho_B(b)\le1$, so step 2 gives $j(f_h)\in A_{\le1}$. Thus $b=\sum_h\varphi(j(f_h))y_h$ is in the $A_{\le1}$-span of the finite family $y_h\in B_{\le1}$. Conversely each such finite combination belongs to $B_{\le1}$ by spectral contraction of $\varphi$, submultiplicativity and the ultrametric inequality from step 1. Therefore this family generates exactly $B_{\le1}$ over $A_{\le1}$. This proves module finiteness even when $A$ has nilpotents or $\ker\varphi\ne0$.
